blocks.text: The UGE GP8212S module generates a standard 4–20 mA current loop from an I²C command. Use it to drive industrial inputs on PLCs, inverters, valves, sensors, and other 4–20 mA receivers.

The board uses a GP8212S-TC50-EW 15-bit DAC. With the onboard sense resistor, the full scale is 0–25 mA. The usual industrial range is 4–20 mA. A 5 V supply feeds an MT3608 boost converter that raises the DAC supply to about 12 V, so the module can be powered from USB or a 5 V Arduino pin.

Connect SDA, SCL, 5 V, and GND to an Arduino Uno or ESP32. Put the loop load on the screw-terminal output. A ~330 Ω, 1 W resistor is a good calibration load at 12 V. The Arduino library sets the current in milliamps, as a percent of the 4–20 mA span, or as a raw DAC code.

blocks.text: Using the WCH DAP Link with the STM32F103C8 microcontroller and Keil IDE is straightforward. Below is a step-by-step guide to help you set it up and start debugging/programming your STM32F103C8:
Connect the WCH DAP Link V2 to your STM32F103C8:
Connect the SWDIO pin of the WCH DAP Link V2 to the SWDIO pin (PA13) of the STM32F103C8.
Connect the SWCLK pin of the WCH DAP Link V2 to the SWCLK pin (PA14) of the STM32F103C8.
Connect the GND pin of the WCH DAP Link V2 to the GND pin of the STM32F103C8.
Connect the 3.3V pin of the WCH DAP Link V2 to the 3.3V pin of the STM32F103C8 (if needed for power).
Connect the WCH DAP Link to your PC:
Use the USB-C cable to connect the WCH DAP Link to your computer.
If you haven’t already, download and install the latest version of Keil µVision IDE from the Keil website.
Open Keil IDE and go to Pack Installer (click the puzzle piece icon or navigate via Project > Manage > Pack Installer).
Search for STM32F1 Series Device Family Pack and install it.
Install WCH DAP Link Drivers (if required):
Most operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS) will recognize the WCH DAP Link V2 automatically. If not, download the drivers from the WCH website.
Step 3: Configure Keil IDE for WCH DAP Link
Open Keil IDE and create a new project or open an existing one for the STM32F103C8.
Go to Project > Options for Target (or press Alt + F7).
Select CMSIS-DAP Debugger from the dropdown menu under “Use.”
Click on Settings next to the debugger dropdown.
In the Debug tab, ensure the following:
Ensure the Reset and Run option is checked.
Add the STM32F1xx Flash algorithm (it should be available if you installed the STM32F1 device pack).
Click on Verify in the debug settings to ensure the WCH DAP Link is properly connected to the STM32F103C8.
Step 4: Build and Flash the Firmware
Click on Build (or press F7) to compile your project.
Click on Download (or press F8) to flash the firmware to the STM32F103C8.
Click on Debug (or press Ctrl + F5) to start a debugging session.
Use Keil’s debugging tools (breakpoints, watch windows, etc.) to debug your code.
Click on Run (or press F5) to execute the program on the STM32F103C8.

blocks.text: A capacitor (originally known as a condenser) is a passive two-terminal electrical component used to store energyelectrostatically in an electric field. The forms of practical capacitors vary widely, but all contain at least two electrical conductors (plates) separated by a dielectric (i.e. insulator). The conductors can be thin films, foils or sintered beads of metal or conductive electrolyte, etc. The “nonconducting” dielectric acts to increase the capacitor’s charge capacity. A dielectric can be glass, ceramic, plastic film, air, vacuum, paper, mica, oxide layer etc. Capacitors are widely used as parts of electrical circuits in many common electrical devices. Unlike a resistor, an ideal capacitor does not dissipate energy. Instead, a capacitor stores energy in the form of an electrostatic field between its plates.

When there is a potential difference across the conductors (e.g., when a capacitor is attached across a battery), an electric field develops across the dielectric, causing positive charge +Q to collect on one plate and negative charge −Q to collect on the other plate. If a battery has been attached to a capacitor for a sufficient amount of time, no current can flow through the capacitor. However, if a time-varying voltage is applied across the leads of the capacitor, a displacement current can flow.

An ideal capacitor is characterized by a single constant value for its capacitance. Capacitance is expressed as the ratio of the electric charge Q on each conductor to the potential difference V between them. The SI unit of capacitance is the farad (F), which is equal to one coulomb per volt (1 C/V). Typical capacitance values range from about 1 pF (10−12 F) to about 1 mF (10−3 F).

The capacitance is greater when there is a narrower separation between conductors and when the conductors have a larger surface area. In practice, the dielectric between the plates passes a small amount of leakage current and also has an electric field strength limit, known as the breakdown voltage. The conductors and leads introduce an undesired inductance and resistance.

Capacitors are widely used in electronic circuits for blocking direct current while allowing alternating current to pass. In analog filter networks, they smooth the output of power supplies. In resonant circuits they tune radios to particular frequencies. Inelectric power transmission systems, they stabilize voltage and power flow.

Power the module and provide an input signal.
Observe how the LEDs light up based on the input signal level.

makers-1789.summary: The TIP36C is a 100V, 25A PNP bipolar power transistor in a TO-247 package, featuring high gain and low saturation voltage.

blocks.text: The TIP36C is a PNP bipolar power transistor manufactured using planar technology with a specific “base island” layout. This advanced manufacturing technique is central to the device’s construction, optimizing the internal semiconductor geometry to enhance its power handling capabilities and electrical efficiency. The design is focused on creating a robust and reliable component that serves as the perfect complement to its NPN counterpart.

This transistor is engineered to deliver a powerful combination of high current gain and very low saturation voltage. The exceptional high gain performance means it can control a large output collector current with a relatively smaller base current. The low collector-emitter saturation voltage is a critical feature, as it minimizes power loss and heat generation when the transistor is fully switched on, thereby increasing the overall efficiency of the circuit it is used in.

Housed in a TO-247 package, this device is built for high-power applications where effective thermal management is essential. The robust package allows for significant power dissipation. The TIP36C is explicitly designed as the complementary PNP pair to the NPN TIP35C, enabling designers to construct symmetrical output stages, such as the Class B push-pull configurations found in high-quality audio power amplifiers.
Manufactured in planar technology with “base island” layout.

makers-486515.summary: 256K-bit (32K×8) CMOS EPROM (27C256) fast reads (90 ns option), low power, express programming, multiple packages (DIP/PLCC/SOIC), wide temp ranges.

blocks.text: The 27C256 is a 256-Kbit (32K × 8) CMOS EPROM (one-time programmable) designed for high-speed, low-power read operations. It provides fast, byte-wide access (access times down to 90 ns) so microprocessors can fetch code or data without added wait states. The device is offered in multiple package styles (DIP, PLCC, SOIC) and supports standard JEDEC pinouts for easy board integration.

Built using CMOS technology, the 27C256 minimizes active and standby current draw (typical active ≈20 mA; standby ≈100 µA) while maintaining stable output drive and low leakage. Programming is performed using a VPP programming voltage and an express programming algorithm that applies short program pulses and verifies bytes automatically, improving production throughput. The device also includes separate CE and OE controls to simplify bus sharing and system designs.

The part is robust for long-term storage (data retention >200 years specified) and is available across commercial, industrial and automotive temperature ranges, making it suitable for legacy systems, firmware storage, and environments that require extended temperature operation. Identity mode and programming inhibit features ease manufacturing and parallel programming setups.

The screw-terminal aluminum electrolytic capacitor with a specification of 5600 µF at 450 V is built to deliver robust energy storage and smoothing in demanding high-voltage DC circuits. Its high capacitance and elevated voltage rating combine to accommodate significant energy transients and ripple currents, giving system designers a reliable buffer against voltage fluctuations.

Internally, this type of capacitor contains wound aluminum foil and electrolyte, optimized for low impedance, large charge/discharge capability and durability. The screw terminal design allows straightforward mounting and secure connection in industrial or power-electronics modules, where robust connection and minimal contact resistance matter. Because the voltage rating is 450 V, it can be used in more demanding bus-voltage contexts compared to lower-voltage types, increasing design flexibility.

In operational use, this capacitor serves as a backbone of power conversion systems, uninterruptible power supplies, high-power amplifiers or industrial drives anywhere that energy must be stored, smoothed and delivered reliably under heavy load and long duty cycles. Its rugged construction and high rating allow longer life, better stability and reduced downtime risk. Proper implementation in a circuit minimizes voltage sag, reduces ripple, and helps maintain consistent performance across load changes.

makers-432934.summary: Dual five-input CMOS majority-logic gate with control input, diode-protected I/O, 3–18 V supply, and TTL-drive capability in a 16-pin package.

blocks.text: The MC14530B is a dual five-input majority‐logic gate implemented in CMOS. It evaluates five logic inputs (A–E) and a control input (W), outputting “1” when three or more of A–E are “1,” then gating that result with W. Conversely, it outputs “0” when three or more inputs are “0,” regardless of W. Diode protection on every input guards against static discharge, and the device can directly drive two low-power TTL loads or one low-power Schottky‐TTL load.

Constructed with complementary P-channel and N-channel enhancement-mode MOSFETs, the MC14530B features matched pull-up and pull-down networks for balanced rise/fall times. Its high-impedance inputs accept voltages from –0.5 V up to VDD+0.5 V, while output stages source and sink up to ±10 mA. A wide supply range (3 V to 18 V) allows flexible system integration. Unused inputs must be tied to VSS or VDD; unused outputs remain open.

By embedding majority logic in a single 16-pin package, the MC14530B simplifies both combinational and sequential designs—reducing component count compared to discrete gates. Its protection circuitry and broad voltage tolerance enhance reliability in noisy or mixed-voltage environments. Typical applications include custom flip-flops, multivibrators, and programmable‐logic modules where compact, high-fan-in logic functions are required.

makers-391497.summary: DTM-028K: A high-sensitivity piezoelectric vibration sensor with customizable mass for versatile low-frequency applications.

blocks.text: Precision Vibration Detection: LDTM-028K Piezo Sensor for Advanced Applications

The LDT0-028K is a flexible component comprising a 28 μm thick piezoelectric PVDF polymer film with screen-printed Ag-ink electrodes, laminated to a 0.125 mm polyester substrate, and fitted with two crimped contacts. As the piezo film is displaced from the mechanical neutral axis, bending creates very high strain within the piezopolymer and therefore high voltages are generated. When the assembly is deflected by direct contact, the device acts as a flexible “switch”, and the generated output is sufficient to trigger MOSFET or CMOS stages directly. If the assembly is supported by its contacts and left to vibrate “in free space” (with the inertia of the clamped/free beam creating bending stress), the device will behave as an accelerometer or vibration sensor. Adding mass, or altering the free length of the element by clamping, can change the resonant frequency and sensitivity of the sensor to suit specific applications. The multi-axis response can be achieved by positioning the mass off-center. The LDTM-028K is a vibration sensor where the sensing element comprises a cantilever beam loaded by an additional mass to offer high sensitivity at low frequencies.

The AT28C64B is a high-performance electrically-erasable and programmable read-only memory (EEPROM). Its 64K of memory is organized as 8,192 words by 8 bits. Manufactured with Atmel’s advanced nonvolatile CMOS technology, the device offers access times to 150 ns with power dissipation of just 220 mW. When the device is deselected, the CMOS standby current is less than 100 µA.

The AT28C64B is accessed like a Static RAM for the read or write cycle without the need for external components. The device contains a 64-byte page register to allow writing of up to 64 bytes simultaneously. During a write cycle, the addresses and 1 to 64 bytes of data are internally latched, freeing the address and data bus for other operations. Following the initiation of a write cycle, the device will automatically write the latched data using an internal control timer. The end of a write cycle can be detected by DATA POLLING of I/O7. Once the end of a write cycle has been detected, a new access for a read or write can begin.

Atmel’s AT28C64B has additional features to ensure high quality and manufacturability. The device utilizes internal error correction for extended endurance and improved data retention characteristics. An optional software data protection mechanism is available to guard against inadvertent writes. The device also includes an extra 64 bytes of EEPROM for device identification or tracking.

blocks.text: This circuit is mainly an alarm control circuit formed by the gas sensor group MQ-3. When the sensor MQ-3 is in the environment where alcohol vapor exists, the conductivity of the sensor will be the same as the alcohol vapor concentration. By measuring the series partial pressure between the sensor and the fixed resistor, the alcohol content in the environment can be judged.

This circuit can be powered by 5-7.5V DC power supply, switch S1 is the power switch, resistor R1 and LED D1 are used for power indication. The internal sensor MQ3 needs to be heated to a certain temperature during operation, so its internal installation.

There is a heating wire, the resistor R4 is the current limiting resistor of the heating wire, and the heating of MQ-3 is normal after power-on. When MQ-3 does not detect alcohol vapor, its internal resistance is very large, the voltage drop of R3, RW is very low, the voltage of pin 2 of NE555 is lower than the trigger voltage (VCC/3), its 3 pin output is high level, D2 is extinguished. The buzzer does not sound and the relay does not move.

When MQ-3 detects alcohol vapor, the internal resistance decreases, the voltage of R3, RW rises, the voltage of pin 2 of NE555 is higher than the trigger voltage, the 3 pin becomes low level, D2 turns on the light, and the buzzer flows. The current starts to sound, and the electromagnetic coil in the relay energizes to attract the switch. Thereby implementing the detection alarm function.

The adjustable resistor RW is used to adjust the detection sensitivity. This circuit uses a second comparator inside the NE555 to detect voltage changes, using its internal trigger to debounce. The 7 and 5 feet of the NE555 are not used and are left floating. The output terminal J3 of the relay can be used to control other electrical appliances, such as exhaust fans.

When the alcohol concentration exceeds the standard, the exhaust fan is activated. After the concentration drops, the exhaust fan is turned off to realize automatic control. Diode D3 is used to eliminate the induced electromotive force generated when the relay coil is turned on and off. The power supply interface can be a DC plug, or the line can be directly at the J2 position, pay attention to the positive and negative signs, and the DC plug is internally and externally negative.

blocks.text: Voltage Detection Sensor Module Features & Specifications

The voltage Detection Sensor Module is a simple and very useful module that uses a potential divider to reduce any input voltage by a factor of 5. This allows us to use the Analog input pin of a microcontroller to monitor voltages higher than it capable of sensing. For example, with a 0V – 5V Analog input range, you can measure a voltage up to 25V. This module also includes convenient screw terminals for easy and secure connections of a wire.
The internal circuit diagram of the Voltage Sensor Module is given below.
The voltage circuit consists of a voltage divider circuit of two resistors in which R1 is 30K and R2 is 7.5K.
How to Use Voltage Sensor Module with Arduino

Interfacing a voltage sensor with Arduino or any other microcontroller is pretty straightforward. Connect the VCC and GND of the voltage source whose voltage is to be measured to the screw terminals of the voltage sensor. Connect the S and – (GND) pins of the voltage sensor to the Analog pin and GND of Arduino respectively.
Input and output voltage can be calculated using:
Vin = Vout * (R2/(R1+R2)) Here R1 = 30K ohm and R2 = 7.5K ohm Vout = (analogvalue * 5 / 1024).

blocks.text: The 74162 is a synchronous 4-bit binary counter implemented in the TTL (LS) family. It provides four buffered outputs representing a 4-bit binary value and advances the count synchronously on a common clock edge when the enable inputs are asserted. The device supports parallel-loading of a preset value and a clear function, allowing designers to initialize or force any desired start count without ripple delays. Its internal gating makes all bit changes occur in the same clock transition, which simplifies timing in high-speed or cascaded counting applications.

Architecturally the IC includes parallel data inputs, active-low synchronous load and asynchronous clear pins, two enable inputs (for look-ahead expansion) and a ripple-carry / look-ahead output that lets multiple counters be cascaded for wider counters with predictable timing. Because counting is synchronous, hazards and glitches common to ripple counters are minimized; the outputs change in unison, so system timing and metastability are easier to manage.

Housed in standard 16-pin packages (PDIP, SOIC/SOP, CFP/LCCC variants), the 74162 is suited to TTL-based digital designs where a robust, easy-to-cascade binary counter is needed—for example frequency division, digital sequencing, timed state machines, or address generation in small microcontroller systems. Standard commercial temperature and packaging options are provided by the manufacturer.

makers-1866.summary: The 74LS164 is an 8-bit serial-in, parallel-out shift register used to convert serial data into parallel outputs for digital logic circuits, microcontroller interfaces, and sequential control systems.

blocks.text: 74LS164 Serial to Parallel Counter Shift Register 8-Bit DIP-14

The 74LS164 is an 8-bit serial-in, parallel-out shift register integrated circuit designed to receive data serially and make it available through eight parallel output pins. It shifts the stored data with each active clock transition, making it useful when a digital system needs to expand its output capability or process serial data using parallel logic.

The IC includes two serial data inputs, a clock input, and an asynchronous active-low clear input for resetting the register. Its compact DIP-14 through-hole package makes it suitable for prototyping, educational electronics, digital logic projects, and PCB assembly. Unlike the 74HC595, the standard 74LS164 does not include a separate output latch, so its parallel outputs change as data shifts through the register.
These 8-bit shift registers feature gated serial inputs and an asynchronous clear.
A low logic level at either input inhibits entry of the new data, and resets the first flip-flop to the low level at the next clock pulse, thus providing complete control over incoming data.
A high logic level on either input enables the other input, which will then determine the state of the first flip-flop.
Data at the serial inputs may be changed while the clock is HIGH or LOW, but only information meeting the setup and hold time requirements will be entered.
Clocking occurs on the LOW-to-HIGH level transition of the clock input.
All inputs are diode-clamped to minimize transmission-line effects.
Fully buffered clock and serial inputs.

makers-1767.summary: The IRF520 is a 100V, 9.2A N-Channel HEXFET Power MOSFET in a TO-220 package with a low 0.27Ω on-resistance.

blocks.text: The IRF520 is a third-generation N-channel HEXFET power MOSFET from International Rectifier, representing an advanced design that effectively balances fast switching performance, ruggedness, and low on-resistance. It is engineered using a vertical DMOS structure, which is the foundation of the HEXFET technology, enabling high efficiency and robust power handling. This transistor functions as a voltage-controlled device, where a voltage applied to the gate terminal relative to the source allows current to flow between the drain and source, making it an ideal solid-state switch for power electronics.

This MOSFET is characterized by its ability to switch currents rapidly, which is essential for high-frequency applications like switch-mode power supplies and motor controllers. The device is ruggedized, being rated for repetitive avalanche, meaning it can withstand short periods of over-voltage stress that drive it into the breakdown region without being damaged. This built-in durability, combined with a high operating junction temperature of 175°C, makes it a reliable component in demanding environments.

Housed in the industry-standard TO-220 package, the IRF520 is designed for easy mounting onto heat sinks, which is crucial for dissipating the heat generated during operation. The package offers a low thermal resistance from the silicon junction to the case, allowing the transistor to handle significant power levels. Its simple drive requirements and ease of paralleling make it a versatile and cost-effective choice for a wide range of commercial and industrial power applications.

blocks.text: ESP8266 NodeMcu WiFi Programming & Development Kit With CH340

The ESP8266 NodeMCU WiFi Programming & Development Kit with CH340 is a powerful, open-source development board tailored for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Powered by the ESP8266 WiFi module, it offers seamless wireless connectivity through the 802.11 b/g/n standard, enabling the creation of smart, connected devices. The integrated CH340 USB-to-serial converter facilitates easy programming and debugging via a micro USB cable, eliminating the need for external programmers. Compatible with both Arduino IDE and Lua scripting, this board is ideal for hobbyists, students, and professionals looking to prototype or deploy IoT solutions. Its compact, breadboard-friendly design and robust feature set make it a go-to choice for projects ranging from home automation to wireless sensor networks.

Besides adding WiFi capability, the main claim to fame for the ESP8266 processor over the AVR processor of the standard Arduino is that it has a larger 4 MB of Flash memory and runs at clock speeds of 80 MHz and can sometimes optionally be overclocked to 160 MHz and therefore has a very fast processing speed.

The Digital I/O all support PWM and interrupts. In addition they can be configured to have pull-up or pull-down resistors. Though there are 11 digital I/O pins, 2 are typically reserved for use as the TX/RX lines if serial communications are used which leaves 9 digital I/O.

On the down-side, it has only 1 analog input which is probably the most significant limitation for some sensor type applications. That can always be overcome by using an external Analog Mux module like our 16-channel 74HC4067 or our ADS1115 4-channel 16-bit ADC module below if more analog I/O is desired.

The module can be powered via the USB port or by using an external 7-12V power supply connected to the VIN pin. The module runs at 3.3V, so keep that in mind when working with I/O. The digital I/O is stated as being 5V tolerant, but the analog input needs to be limited to < 3.3V.
The blue on-board LED is connected to D0 (GPIO16) and can be accessed using the LED_BUILTIN constant.

The module has a typical ‘Reset’ button as well as a ‘Flash’ button. The Flash button is used when programming using the original NodeMCU firmware. If the module is being used with the Arduino IDE, the Flash button does not need to be used to program the board and it will program just as any Arduino board would.

The module comes loaded with the NodeMCU software that accepts the standard AT command set. The module was initially designed primarily to be programmed using Lua which is an interpreted language, but Lua has been mostly abandoned because it takes up a lot of memory and is slow because it is interpreted and more importantly it is generally buggy.

It can also be programmed in C using the Arduino IDE and is how the modules are most often used. An example program is shown down below. If a program is download via the IDE, it will overwrite the NodeMCU software or whatever else was loaded before. If that is a problem for what you want to do, the NodeMCU software can always be reloaded.

The board uses the CH340 chip for USB communications. If you have any issues with connecting to the board, you may need to download a driver. Just search for Arduino CH340 driver and you will find a number of sources for drivers depending on what Windows or Mac operating system you are using.

These can be read by almost any 13.56MHz RFID/NFC reader, but make sure it can handle ISO/IEC 14443 Type A cards (the standard NTAG uses) as there are a few other encoding standards (like FeLica).

These chips can be written to and store up to 504 bytes of data in writable EEPROM divided into 4 byte banks, and can handle over 10,000 re-writes. You can use our PN532 NFC/RFID breakout board or NFC/RFID Shield for Arduino to read and write data to the EEPROM inside the tag. There is also a permanent 7-byte serial number ID burned into the chip that you can use to identify one tag from another – the ID number cannot be changed.

These use an NTAG chipset, a ‘Type 2’ tag that is usable with any smartphone. Unlike “Classic 1K” cards (a.k.a MiFare S50s), these tags are more secure and work with almost any phone with RFID support since they avoid the patent issues with Mifare, which requires an NXP chipset or license fee.

TDS (Total Dissolved Solids) indicates that how many milligrams of soluble solids dissolved in one liter of water. In general, the higher the TDS value, the more soluble solids dissolved in water, and the less clean the water is. Therefore, the TDS value can be used as one of the references for reflecting the cleanliness of water.

TDS pen is a widely used equipment to measure TDS value. The price is affordable, and it is easy to use, but it is not able to transmit data to the control system for online monitoring to do some water quality analysis. The professional instrument has high accuracy and can send data to the control system, but the price is expensive for the ordinary people. To this end, we have launched an analog TDS sensor kit which is compatible with forArduino, plug and play, easy to use. Matching with forArduino controller, you can build a TDS detector easily to measure the TDS value of liquid.

This product supports 3.3 ~ 5.5V wide voltage input, and 0 ~ 2.3V analog voltage output, which makes it compatible with 5V or 3.3V control system or board. The excitation source is AC signal, which can effectively prevent the probe from polarization and prolong the life of the probe, meanwhile, increase the stability of the output signal. The TDS probe is waterproof, it can be immersed in water for long time measurement.

This product can be used in water quality application, such as domestic water, hydroponics. With this product, you can easily DIY a TDS detector to reflect the cleanliness of water to protect your health.
1.The probe can not be used in water above 55 degrees centigrade.
2.The probe can not be left too close to the edge of the container, otherwise it will affect the reading.
3.The head and the cable of the probe are waterproof, but the connector and the signal transmitter board are not waterproof. Please be careful.
Good Compatibility Output: 0~2.3V analog signal output, compatible with 5V or 3.3V controller
AC Excitation Source: effectively prevent probe from polarization
Easy to Use: forArduino compatible, simple connection, plug and play without soldering
Gravity: Analog TDS Sensor/Meter for Arduino x1

electrohub-15173.summary: كيت Arduino UNO R3 SMD متكامل لتعلّم الإلكترونيات والبرمجة وتنفيذ المشاريع العملية. يحتوي على لوحة أردوينو، وبريدبورد، ومكونات إلكترونية متنوعة، وشاشات عرض، ومستشعرات، ومحرك سيرفو، وأدوات للتحكم في المحركات. مثالي للطلاب والمبتدئين وهواة الإلكترونيات والروبوتات لبناء مشاريعهم والتعلم بالتجربة.

blocks.text: كيت أردوينو UNO R3 SMD للمبتدئين – مستشعرات وشاشات وتحكم في المحركات

كيت إلكترونيات متكامل للتعلم والتجربة باستخدام الأردوينو، يحتوي على لوحة Arduino UNO R3 SMD، ولوحة تجارب كبيرة، ومكونات إلكترونية متنوعة، وشاشات عرض، ومستشعرات، ومحرك سيرفو، وأدوات للتحكم في المحركات. مناسب للطلاب والمبتدئين وهواة الإلكترونيات لتنفيذ المشاريع العملية وتعلم البرمجة والإلكترونيات خطوة بخطوة.
ابدأ رحلتك في عالم الإلكترونيات والبرمجة مع كيت Arduino UNO R3 SMD، الذي يجمع مجموعة متنوعة من المكونات الأساسية اللازمة لتصميم الدوائر الإلكترونية وتنفيذ مشاريع الأردوينو العملية.
يساعدك هذا الكيت على تعلم أساسيات البرمجة، والتحكم في الإضاءة، وقراءة بيانات المستشعرات، وعرض المعلومات على الشاشات، وتجربة التحكم في المحركات والحركة.
سواء كنت مبتدئًا في مجال الإلكترونيات أو ترغب في تنفيذ مشروعات تعليمية وتطبيقية، يوفر لك هذا الكيت نقطة بداية مناسبة للتعلم والتجربة.
التحكم والبرمجة: لوحة Arduino UNO R3 SMD لتنفيذ البرامج والتحكم في المكونات الإلكترونية.
تجميع الدوائر الإلكترونية: لوحة تجارب 830 نقطة، وكابل USB، وأسلاك توصيل، وليدات ملونة، ومقاومات، وأزرار ضغط.
شاشات العرض: شاشة LCD مقاس 16×2 وشاشة 7-Segment لعرض النصوص والأرقام.
المستشعرات: مستشعر الموجات فوق الصوتية HC-SR04 لقياس المسافات، ومستشعر الضوء LDR، ومستشعر الأشعة تحت الحمراء لاكتشاف العوائق.
التحكم عن بُعد: ريموت ومستقبل أشعة تحت الحمراء للتحكم في المشروعات لاسلكيًا.
التحكم في الحركة: محرك سيرفو SG90 وArduino Motor Shield لتجربة تطبيقات التحكم في المحركات والحركة.
ليدات LED بالألوان الأصفر والأخضر والأحمر.

أسلاك توصيل ذكر إلى ذكر (Male to Male).
مقاومة متغيرة Potentiometer بقيمة 10 كيلو أوم.
ريموت تحكم ومستقبل أشعة تحت الحمراء.

مستشعر الأشعة تحت الحمراء لاكتشاف العوائق.
التحكم في إضاءة الليدات باستخدام الأردوينو.
قياس المسافات باستخدام المستشعر فوق الصوتي.
اكتشاف العوائق باستخدام مستشعر الأشعة تحت الحمراء.
تجربة التحكم في زاوية حركة محرك السيرفو.
مناسب لطلاب المدارس والجامعات، والمبتدئين في الإلكترونيات، وهواة البرمجة والروبوتات، وكل من يرغب في تعلم الأردوينو من خلال التجارب والمشروعات العملية.
كيت متكامل يساعدك على تحويل أفكارك إلى مشروعات إلكترونية حقيقية، والتعلم بالتجربة والتطبيق.

The 4S 40A Lithium Battery BMS Protection Board (Balance Charging) is a battery management circuit designed to protect four-cell (4S) lithium-ion or LiFePO4 packs from common failure conditions while balancing charge across the cells during use. It suits DIY power banks, e-bike packs and portable tool battery packs.
Cell Configuration: Designed for 4S lithium battery packs at a 14.8V nominal pack voltage.
Continuous Current: Rated for up to 40A of continuous charge and discharge current.
Overcharge & Overdischarge Protection: Automatically disconnects the pack when any cell exceeds safe voltage limits.
Cell Balancing: Built-in balancing circuitry helps equalize voltage across all four cells during charging.
Short-Circuit Protection: Cuts power instantly if a short circuit is detected on the output.
Compact PCB: Small footprint fits easily inside battery packs and enclosures.
It’s a practical safety layer for any 4S lithium pack built from 18650 or similar cells.

The STI8036 LNB Power Supply & Control Voltage Regulator IC (SOP-8) is a monolithic boost converter and linear regulator that powers a satellite dish LNB (low-noise block downconverter) from a set-top box or satellite receiver. It supplies the switched 14V/19V rail and 22kHz tone signal used to select LNB polarity and band.
Dual Output Voltage: Switches between a regulated 14V and 19V output to select LNB polarity.
22kHz Tone Injection: Generates the 22kHz tone signal used for LNB band switching and DiSEqC-style control.
Integrated Boost Converter: Combines a DC/DC boost stage with a low-noise linear regulator on a single chip.
500mA Output Current: Delivers enough current to power a standard single or twin LNB.
Compact SOP-8 Package: Small surface-mount footprint drops directly into existing satellite receiver and STB PCB designs.
Built-In Protection: Includes thermal shutdown and current-limit protection for reliable field operation.
A common repair and replacement part for satellite receivers, set-top boxes and satellite TV cards.

The 3S 40A 12V Lithium Battery Protection Module (BMS) with Balancing is a higher-current battery management circuit for 3-series (11.1V/12.6V) lithium-ion or Li-Po packs, protecting against overcharge, overdischarge, and overcurrent while balancing all three cells during charging. Its larger MOSFET bank suits higher-drain packs such as those used in power tools and e-bikes.
Overcharge/Overdischarge Protection: Automatically disconnects the pack when any cell exceeds its safe voltage window.
Passive Cell Balancing: Bleeds excess charge from higher-voltage cells so all three stay closely matched.
40A Continuous Current: An expanded MOSFET bank supports sustained discharge currents up to 40A.
Short-Circuit Protection: Cuts off the output instantly if a short circuit is detected on the load side.
Compact Green PCB: A small footprint fits neatly inside battery packs and power tool housings.
Simple Wiring: Labeled pads for each cell tap plus main positive and negative terminals simplify installation.
Wire each cell tap to its matching pad in series order and route the pack’s main leads through the P+ and P- terminals to keep a higher-drain 3S lithium pack protected during charge and discharge.
